claim: Mutations in the TRPV4 ion channel can lead to a range of skeletal dysplasias.
source: Mutations in the TRPV4 ion channel can lead to a range of skeletal dysplasias.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the subsequent detailed findings in the manuscript.

claim: hiPSC-derived chondrocytes with the V620I mutation exhibited increased basal currents through TRPV4.
source: We found that hiPSC-derived chondrocytes with the V620I mutation exhibited increased basal currents through TRPV4.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiology data presented in Figure 1A-B showing higher basal currents in V620I.

claim: Both V620I and T89I mutations showed more rapid calcium signaling with a reduced overall magnitude in response to TRPV4 agonist GSK1016790A compared to wildtype.
source: However, both mutations showed more rapid calcium signaling with a reduced overall magnitude in response to TRPV4 agonist GSK1016790A compared to wildtype (WT).
evidence: This is supported by confocal imaging and patch clamping data shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: There were no differences in overall cartilaginous matrix production among WT, V620I, and T89I cell lines.
source: There were no differences in overall cartilaginous matrix production, but the V620I mutation resulted in reduced mechanical properties of cartilage matrix later in chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assays showing similar sGAG/DNA ratios across cell lines (Figure 2E).

claim: The V620I mutation resulted in reduced mechanical properties of cartilage matrix later in chondrogenesis.
source: There were no differences in overall cartilaginous matrix production, but the V620I mutation resulted in reduced mechanical properties of cartilage matrix later in chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by AFM measurements showing decreased elastic modulus in V620I at day 42 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2–1B).

claim: Both V620I and T89I mutations up-regulated several anterior HOX genes throughout chondrogenesis.
source: mRNA sequencing revealed that both mutations up-regulated several anterior HOX genes and down-regulated antioxidant genes CAT and GSTA1 throughout chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data showing increased expression of HOXA2-7, HOXB2-4 in mutants (Figure 4I).

claim: Both V620I and T89I mutations down-regulated antioxidant genes CAT and GSTA1 throughout chondrogenesis.
source: mRNA sequencing revealed that both mutations up-regulated several anterior HOX genes and down-regulated antioxidant genes CAT and GSTA1 throughout chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data showing decreased expression of CAT and GSTA1 in mutants (Figure 4F).

claim: BMP4 treatment up-regulated several essential hypertrophic genes in WT chondrocytes.
source: BMP4 treatment up-regulated several essential hypertrophic genes in WT chondrocytes; however, this hypertrophic maturation response was inhibited in mutant chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and RNA sequencing data showing increased expression of COL10A1, ALPL, IHH, RUNX2 in WT with BMP4 treatment (Figure 5C).

claim: The hypertrophic maturation response to BMP4 was inhibited in mutant chondrocytes.
source: BMP4 treatment up-regulated several essential hypertrophic genes in WT chondrocytes; however, this hypertrophic maturation response was inhibited in mutant chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and histological data showing reduced hypertrophic marker expression and cell size in mutants compared to WT (Figure 5A-C).

claim: TRPV4 mutations alter BMP signaling in chondrocytes and prevent proper chondrocyte hypertrophy.
source: These results indicate that the TRPV4 mutations alter BMP signaling in chondrocytes and prevent proper chondrocyte hypertrophy, as a potential mechanism for dysfunctional skeletal development.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the BMP4 treatment experiments showing differential responses between WT and mutant cells.

claim: Skeletal dysplasias comprise a heterogeneous group of over 450 bone and cartilage diseases with an overall birth incidence of 1 in 5000.
source: Skeletal dysplasias comprise a heterogeneous group of over 450 bone and cartilage diseases with an overall birth incidence of 1 in 5000 (Krakow and Rimoin, 2010; Nemec et al., 2012; Ngo et al., 2018; Orioli et al., 1986; Superti-Furga and Unger, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: A V620I substitution (exon 12, G858A) in TRPV4 is responsible for moderate brachyolmia.
source: For example, a V620I substitution (exon 12, G858A) in TRPV4 is responsible for moderate brachyolmia, which exhibits short stature, scoliosis, and delayed development of deformed bones (Kang et al., 2012; Rock et al., 2008; Kang, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Moderate brachyolmia exhibits short stature, scoliosis, and delayed development of deformed bones.
source: For example, a V620I substitution (exon 12, G858A) in TRPV4 is responsible for moderate brachyolmia, which exhibits short stature, scoliosis, and delayed development of deformed bones (Kang et al., 2012; Rock et al., 2008; Kang, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature describing the clinical phenotype.

claim: Metatropic dysplasia can be caused by a TRPV4 T89I substitution (exon 2, C366T).
source: Metatropic dysplasia can be caused by a TRPV4 T89I substitution (exon 2, C366T) and leads to joint contractures, disproportionate measurements, and, in severe cases, neonatal death due to small chest size and cardiopulmonary compromise (Camacho et al., 2010; Kang et al., 2012; Kang, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Metatropic dysplasia leads to joint contractures, disproportionate measurements, and, in severe cases, neonatal death due to small chest size and cardiopulmonary compromise.
source: Metatropic dysplasia can be caused by a TRPV4 T89I substitution (exon 2, C366T) and leads to joint contractures, disproportionate measurements, and, in severe cases, neonatal death due to small chest size and cardiopulmonary compromise (Camacho et al., 2010; Kang et al., 2012; Kang, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature describing the clinical phenotype.

claim: Both V620I and T89I TRPV4 mutations are considered gain-of-function variants.
source: Both V620I and T89I TRPV4 mutations are considered gain-of-function variants (Leddy et al., 2014b; Loukin et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: TRPV4 plays an essential role during chondrogenesis.
source: Given the essential role of TRPV4 during chondrogenesis (Muramatsu et al., 2007; Willard et al., 2021) and cartilage homeostasis (O'Conor et al., 2014), it is hypothesized that TRPV4 mutations may affect endochondral ossification during skeletal development.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: TRPV4 plays a role in cartilage homeostasis.
source: Given the essential role of TRPV4 during chondrogenesis (Muramatsu et al., 2007; Willard et al., 2021) and cartilage homeostasis (O'Conor et al., 2014), it is hypothesized that TRPV4 mutations may affect endochondral ossification during skeletal development.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Endochondral ossification is a process by which bone tissue is created from a cartilage template.
source: Endochondral ossification is a process by which bone tissue is created from a cartilage template (Breeland et al., 2021; Camacho et al., 2010; Krakow and Rimoin, 2010; Rimoin et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: During endochondral ossification, chondrocytes transition from maintaining the homeostasis of cartilage, regulated by transcription factor SOX9, to hypertrophy.
source: During this process, chondrocytes transition from maintaining the homeostasis of cartilage, regulated by transcription factor SRY-box containing gene 9 (SOX9) (Breeland et al., 2021; Nishimura et al., 2012b; Prein and Beier, 2019; Sophia Fox et al., 2009), to hypertrophy.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Hypertrophy is driven by RUNX2 and BMP signaling.
source: Hypertrophy is driven by runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) and bone morphogenic protein (BMP) signaling (Breeland et al., 2021; Nishimura et al., 2012b; Prein and Beier, 2019) and leads to chondrocyte apoptosis or differentiation into osteoblasts to form bone (Breeland et al., 2021; Nishimura et al., 2012b; Prein and Beier, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Hypertrophy leads to chondrocyte apoptosis or differentiation into osteoblasts to form bone.
source: Hypertrophy is driven by runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) and bone morphogenic protein (BMP) signaling (Breeland et al., 2021; Nishimura et al., 2012b; Prein and Beier, 2019) and leads to chondrocyte apoptosis or differentiation into osteoblasts to form bone (Breeland et al., 2021; Nishimura et al., 2012b; Prein and Beier, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: The activation of TRPV4 increases SOX9 expression.
source: The activation of TRPV4 increases SOX9 expression (Muramatsu et al., 2007) and prevents chondrocyte hypertrophy and endochondral ossification (Amano et al., 2009; Hattori et al., 2010; Lui et al., 2019; Nishimura et al., 2012a; Nishimura et al., 2012b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The activation of TRPV4 prevents chondrocyte hypertrophy and endochondral ossification.
source: The activation of TRPV4 increases SOX9 expression (Muramatsu et al., 2007) and prevents chondrocyte hypertrophy and endochondral ossification (Amano et al., 2009; Hattori et al., 2010; Lui et al., 2019; Nishimura et al., 2012a; Nishimura et al., 2012b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Overexpressing wildtype Trpv4 in mouse embryos increased intracellular calcium concentration and delayed bone mineralization.
source: One study found that overexpressing wildtype (WT) Trpv4 in mouse embryos increased intracellular calcium (Ca2+) concentration and delayed bone mineralization (Weinstein et al., 2014), a potential link between intracellular Ca2+, such as with gain-of-function TRPV4 mutations, and delayed endochondral ossification.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Porcine chondrocytes overexpressing human V620I- and T89I-TRPV4 showed increased expression of follistatin (FST) and delayed hypertrophy.
source: Our previous study also observed increased expression of follistatin (FST), a potent BMP inhibitor, and delayed hypertrophy in porcine chondrocytes overexpressing human V620I- and T89I-TRPV4 (Leddy et al., 2014a; Leddy et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the authors' previous published work.

claim: V620I-TRPV4 had the highest basal currents at both 70 and −70 mV compared to WT and T89I.
source: V620I-TRPV4 had the highest basal currents at both 70 and −70 mV (70/−70 mV pA/pF – WT: 18.52/5.93 vs. V602I: 77.79/55.33 vs. T89I: 40.97/50.13; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-cell patch clamping data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: When TRPV4 was inhibited with GSK205, the three lines had similar, decreased currents.
source: However, when TRPV4 was inhibited with GSK205 (Kanju et al., 2016), a TRPV4-specfic chemical antagonist, the three lines had similar, decreased currents (70/−70 mV – WT: 18.72/14.36 pA/pF vs. V620I: 13.55/9.15 pA/pF vs. T89I: 29.27/13.8 pA/pF; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-cell patch clamping data with GSK205 treatment presented in Figure 1A.

claim: TRPV4 inhibition caused a significant change in current in V620I at both 70 and −70 mV.
source: TRPV4 inhibition caused a significant change in current in V620I at both 70 and −70 mV (70 mV – V620I: Δ64.28 vs. WT: Δ –0.19, p = 0.0379 and T89I: Δ11.67, p < 0.0001; −70 mV – V620I: Δ46.13 vs. WT: Δ −8.47, p < 0.0001 and T89I: Δ36.33, p = 0.0057; Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of patch clamping data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: T89I-TRPV4 was not significantly different from WT in terms of current change with TRPV4 inhibition despite also causing a gain-of-function in recombinant channels.
source: Interestingly, T89I-TRPV4 was not significantly different from WT despite also causing a gain-of-function in recombinant channels (Loukin et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by the patch clamping data in the current study and a citation to published literature about recombinant channels.

claim: WT cells had significantly higher fluorescence, and therefore Ca2+ signaling, in response to GSK101 compared to V620I and T89I.
source: WT cells had significantly higher fluorescence, and therefore Ca2+ signaling, in response to GSK101 according to the plots and their area under the curve (WT: 1470 vs. V620I: 1114 and T89I: 1044; p < 0.0001; Figure 1D, E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data of Ca2+ signaling presented in Figure 1D-E.

claim: The presence of GSK205 attenuated the Ca2+ response to GSK101 for all three lines.
source: The presence of GSK205 attenuated this response for all three lines, confirming the Ca2+ influx was due to the TRPV4 ion channel (WT: 366 vs. V620I: 460 vs. T89I: 358).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data showing reduced Ca2+ signaling with GSK205 treatment.

claim: The mutants responded faster to GSK101 than the WT.
source: The mutants responded faster to GSK101 than the WT (WT: 46.2 s vs. V620I: 12 s, p = 0.0048 and T89I: 10.8 s, p = 0.0097; Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of response time from confocal imaging data presented in Figure 1F.

claim: The addition of GSK205 did not significantly slow the response of WT, but it did slow the response of the mutants.
source: Interestingly, the addition of GSK205 did not significantly slow the response of WT, but it did slow the response of the mutants, with the severe mutation slower than the moderate (WT: 35.4 s vs. V620I: 234 s and T89: 366 s; p < 0.0001; Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of response time with GSK205 treatment from confocal imaging data presented in Figure 1F.

claim: At day 28, the three lines had similar chondrogenic matrix as shown with Safranin-O staining for sulfated glycosaminoglycans and COL2A1 labeling with immunohistochemistry.
source: At day 28, the three lines had similar chondrogenic matrix as shown with Safranin-O staining for sulfated glycosaminoglycans (sGAGs) and collagen type 2 alpha chain 1 (COL2A1) labeling with immunohistochemistry (IHC; Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological images presented in Figure 2A-B.

claim: All three lines had little to no labeling of fibrocartilage marker COL1A1 and hypertrophic cartilage marker COL10A1 with IHC at day 28.
source: All three lines had little to no labeling of fibrocartilage marker COL1A1 and hypertrophic cartilage marker COL10A1 with IHC (Figure 2C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry images presented in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The sGAG/DNA ratio increased in WT by 8-fold and in V620I and T89I by 5- to 5.5-fold from day 14 to 28.
source: The sGAG/DNA ratio increased in WT by 8-fold and in V620I and T89I by 5- to 5.5-fold from day 14 to 28 (p < 0.0001; Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by biochemical assay data presented in Figure 2E.

claim: There were no differences in sGAG/DNA ratios among the three cell lines at any time point.
source: However, there were no differences in sGAG/DNA ratios among the three cell lines at any time point (cell line: p = 0.1206; interaction: p = 0.7426; Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of biochemical assay data presented in Figure 2E.

claim: At day 28, the three lines had similar elastic modulus ranging from 14 to 20 kPa.
source: The elastic modulus ranged from 14 to 20 kPa, consistent with mouse iPSC-derived cartilage (Diekman et al., 2012). At day 28, the three lines had similar properties (WT: 14.4 kPa vs. V620I: 15.9 kPa vs. T89I: 14.8 kPa; Figure 2F)
evidence: This claim is supported by AFM measurements presented in Figure 2F.

claim: At day 42, V620I had a significantly decreased elastic modulus compared to WT and T89I.
source: however, at day 42, V620I had a significantly decreased elastic modulus (V620I: 10.32 kPa vs. WT: 20.0 kPa, p = 0.0004 and T89I: 17.5 kPa, p = 0.0328; Figure 2—figure supplement 2–1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by AFM measurements presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 2–1B.

claim: Mutants had higher ACAN expression compared to WT at day 28.
source: Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) analysis throughout differentiation shows that mutants had higher ACAN expression compared to WT at day 28 (day-28 fold changes; WT: 2314 vs. V620I: 6418, p = 0.1092 and T89I: 5870, p = 0.0316; Figure 3A)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3A.

claim: COL2A1 expression was similar among the three lines at day 28.
source: COL2A1 expression was similar among the three lines at day 28 (day-28 fold changes; WT: 6492 vs. V620I: 6524, p > 0.9999 and T89I: 8131, p = 0.3304; Figure 3B)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3B.

claim: V620I significantly increased expression of chondrogenic transcription factor SOX9 throughout chondrogenesis.
source: Throughout chondrogenesis, V620I significantly increased expression of chondrogenic transcription factor SOX9 (day-28 fold changes; V620I: 178.9 vs. WT: 49.16, p = 0.0011 and T89I: 55.37, p = 0.0117; Figure 3C)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3C.

claim: V620I significantly increased expression of TRPV4 throughout chondrogenesis.
source: Throughout chondrogenesis, V620I significantly increased expression of chondrogenic transcription factor SOX9 (day-28 fold changes; V620I: 178.9 vs. WT: 49.16, p = 0.0011 and T89I: 55.37, p = 0.0117; Figure 3C) and TRPV4 (day-28 fold changes; V620I: 112.1 vs. WT: 42.14, p < 0.0001 and T89I: 45.82, p = 0.0002; Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3D.

claim: T89I significantly increased expression of pro-inflammatory, calcium-binding protein S100B throughout chondrogenesis.
source: On the other hand, T89I significantly increased expression of pro-inflammatory, calcium-binding protein S100B (Yammani, 2012) throughout chondrogenesis (day-28 fold changes; T89I: 2552 vs. WT: 415.8, p < 0.0001 and V620I: 633.6, p = 0.0019; Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3E.

claim: T89I had significantly higher expression of fibrocartilage marker COL1A1 at days 7, 14, and 28 than the other two lines.
source: T89I also had significantly higher expression of fibrocartilage marker COL1A1 at days 7, 14, and 28 than the other two lines (day-28 fold changes; T89I: 80.33 vs. WT: 13.15, p < 0.0001 and V620I: 23.61, p = 0.0043; Figure 3F)
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3F.

claim: Hypertrophic marker COL10A1 was significantly higher in the WT line than the mutants at days 28 and 42.
source: In contrast, hypertrophic marker COL10A1 was significantly higher in the WT line than the mutants at days 28 and 42 (day-28 fold changes; WT: 310.4 vs. V620I: 30.26, p = 0.0338 and T89I: 52.92, p = 0.0033; Figure 3G; Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: There was no significant increase in follistatin (FST) expression in mutants at later time points.
source: Surprisingly, there was no significant increase in follistatin (FST) expression in mutants at later time points (day-28 fold changes; WT: 0.7042 vs. V620I: 0.4025, p = 0.6228 and T89I: 0.4242, p > 0.9999; Figure 3H) despite previous findings (Leddy et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data presented in Figure 3H and contrasts with previous published findings.

claim: The mutants had increased expression of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP), collagen type VI alpha chains 1 and 3 (COL6A1, COL6A3), growth differentiation factor 5 (GDF5), high-temperature requirement A serine peptidase 1 (HTRA1), and secreted protein acidic and cysteine rich (SPARC).
source: While many chondrogenic and hypertrophic genes had similar levels of expression between the lines, the mutants had increased expression of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein (COMP), collagen type VI alpha chains 1 and 3 (COL6A1, COL6A3), growth differentiation factor 5 (GDF5), high-temperature requirement A serine peptidase 1 (HTRA1), and secreted protein acidic and cysteine rich (SPARC) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: The mutations up-regulated expression levels of bone morphogenic protein 6 (BMP6), transforming growth factor 3 (TGFB3), nuclear factor of activated T-Cells C2 (NFATC2), Twist family BHLH transcription factor 1 (TWIST1), ADAM metallopeptidase with thrombospondin type 1 motif 4 (ADAMTS4), and WNT3A.
source: Additionally, the mutations up-regulated expression levels of bone morphogenic protein 6 (BMP6), transforming growth factor 3 (TGFB3), nuclear factor of activated T-Cells C2 (NFATC2), Twist family BHLH transcription factor 1 (TWIST1), ADAM metallopeptidase with thrombospondin type 1 motif 4 (ADAMTS4), and WNT3A (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: The mutants had decreased expression of hypertrophic markers COL10A1, secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), and alkaline phosphatase, biomineralization associated (ALPL).
source: In contrast, the mutants had decreased expression of hypertrophic markers COL10A1, secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), and alkaline phosphatase, biomineralization associated (ALPL) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: The mutations down-regulated osteoblastogenesis transcription factors SOX2 and SOX11.
source: The mutations also down-regulated osteoblastogenesis transcription factors SOX2 and SOX11 and previously identified genes governing off-target differentiation during hiPSC chondrogenesis including nestin (NES), orthodenticle homeobox 2 (OTX2), WNT7A, and WNT7B (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: The mutations down-regulated genes governing off-target differentiation during hiPSC chondrogenesis including nestin (NES), orthodenticle homeobox 2 (OTX2), WNT7A, and WNT7B.
source: The mutations also down-regulated osteoblastogenesis transcription factors SOX2 and SOX11 and previously identified genes governing off-target differentiation during hiPSC chondrogenesis including nestin (NES), orthodenticle homeobox 2 (OTX2), WNT7A, and WNT7B (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: V620I had 8% fewer DEGs than T89I at day 28.
source: In terms of total differentially expressed genes (DEGs) compared to WT, V620I had 8% fewer DEGs than T89I (2459 vs. 2671; Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing analysis presented in Figure 4D.

claim: Mutants had only about half of the number of up-regulated genes compared to down-regulated genes.
source: Mutants had only about half of the number of up-regulated genes compared to down-regulated genes (V620I: 884 vs. 1575, T89I: 978 vs. 1693; Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing analysis presented in Figure 4D.

claim: The majority of the down-regulated DEGs were shared between the two mutants when compared to WT, comprising 76% and 71% of V620I's and T89I's total down-regulated DEGs, respectively.
source: The majority of the down-regulated DEGs were shared between the two mutants when compared to WT, comprising 76% and 71% of V620I's and T89I's total down-regulated DEGs, respectively (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis of RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4E.

claim: The top 25 most down-regulated DEGs for each line included antioxidant catalase (CAT), anti-inflammatory nucleotide-binding and leucine-rich repeat receptor family pyrin domain containing 2 (NLRP2), and Kruppel-like factor 8 (KLF8).
source: We plotted the top 25 most down-regulated DEGs for each line in a heatmap. These included antioxidant catalase (CAT), anti-inflammatory nucleotide-binding and leucine-rich repeat receptor family pyrin domain containing 2 (NLRP2), and Kruppel-like factor 8 (KLF8) (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4F.

claim: Many of the down-regulated DEGs, both unique and shared between V620I and T89I, were associated with Gene Ontology terms related to nervous system development, including many potassium channel genes.
source: Interestingly, many of the down-regulated DEGs, both unique and shared between V620I and T89I, were associated with Gene Ontology (GO) terms related to nervous system development, including many potassium channel genes (i.e., KCN family; Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4G.

claim: 686 up-regulated DEGs were shared by both mutants, while 22% of V620I's and 30% of T89I's up-regulated DEGs were unique to each mutation.
source: In contrast, 686 up-regulated DEGs were shared by both mutants, while 22% of V620I's and 30% of T89I's up-regulated DEGs were unique to each mutation (198 vs. 292; Figure 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis of RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4H.

claim: Several homeobox (HOX) genes were highly expressed in chondrocytes with the TRPV4 mutations, including HOXA2 to HOXA7, HOXA-AS2, HOXB2 to HOXB4, and HOXB-AS1.
source: A heatmap of the top 25 up-regulated DEGs showed that several homeobox (HOX) genes were highly expressed in chondrocytes with the TRPV4 mutations (Figure 4I). These included HOXA2 to HOXA7, HOXA-AS2, HOXB2 to HOXB4, and HOXB-AS1, which are associated with morphogenesis and anterior patterning (Seifert et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4I.

claim: The up-regulated HOX genes are associated with morphogenesis and anterior patterning.
source: A heatmap of the top 25 up-regulated DEGs showed that several homeobox (HOX) genes were highly expressed in chondrocytes with the TRPV4 mutations (Figure 4I). These included HOXA2 to HOXA7, HOXA-AS2, HOXB2 to HOXB4, and HOXB-AS1, which are associated with morphogenesis and anterior patterning (Seifert et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature and RNA sequencing data.

claim: The shared, up-regulated DEGs between two mutants are associated with extracellular matrix production and organization and growth factor binding in GO term analysis.
source: Furthermore, the shared, up-regulated DEGs between two mutants are associated with extracellular matrix production and organization and growth factor binding in GO term analysis, while V620I genes were associated with type I interferon (Figure 4J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4J.

claim: V620I up-regulated genes were associated with type I interferon.
source: Furthermore, the shared, up-regulated DEGs between two mutants are associated with extracellular matrix production and organization and growth factor binding in GO term analysis, while V620I genes were associated with type I interferon (Figure 4J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4J.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations or overexpression of HOXA2, HOXA3, and HOXA4 impair chondrogenesis, limit skeletal development, decrease endochondral ossification regulators, and delay mineralization in animal models.
source: Interestingly, gain-of-function mutations or overexpression of HOXA2, HOXA3, and HOXA4 impair chondrogenesis, limit skeletal development, decrease endochondral ossification regulators, and delay mineralization in animal models (Creuzet et al., 2002; Deprez et al., 2013; Kanzler et al., 1998; Li and Cao, 2006; Massip et al., 2007; Seifert et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: HOXA5 mutations showed disordered patterning of limb bud development.
source: HOXA5 was also highly up-regulated at both days 28 and 56, and mutations in this gene showed disordered patterning of limb bud development (Pineault and Wellik, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: HOXA4 to HOXA7 are associated with rib and spine patterning, and alterations in expression have led to defects.
source: Finally, the rib and spine phenotypes associated with brachyolmia and metatropic dysplasia could be contributed to the altered expression of HOXA4 to HOXA7 as it has been shown that these genes are associated with rib and spine patterning, and alterations in expression have led to defects (Chen et al., 1998; Wellik, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: 74% of V620I up-regulated DEGs, but only 24% of T89I DEGs, were shared between the two lines at day 56.
source: 74% of V620I up-regulated DEGs, but only 24% of T89I DEGs, were shared between the two lines (424 total genes; Figure 4M).
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis of RNA sequencing data presented in Figure 4M.

claim: BMP4-treated WT had developed a more hypertrophic phenotype compared to TGFβ3- and TGFβ3 + BMP4-treated pellets with enlarged chondrocytes at day 56.
source: At day 56, Safranin-O staining indicated the BMP4-treated WT had developed a more hypertrophic phenotype compared to TGFβ3- and TGFβ3 + BMP4-treated pellets with enlarged chondrocytes (cell diameter; WT-BMP4: 27.6 µm vs. WT-TGFβ3: 11.8 µm, V620I-BMP4: 12.5 µm, and T89I-BMP4: 11.3 µm; p < 0.0001; Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis and cell size measurements presented in Figure 5A-B.

claim: The hypertrophic phenotype with enlarged chondrocytes was not present in any of the groups from the V620I and T89I lines.
source: At day 56, Safranin-O staining indicated the BMP4-treated WT had developed a more hypertrophic phenotype compared to TGFβ3- and TGFβ3 + BMP4-treated pellets with enlarged chondrocytes (cell diameter; WT-BMP4: 27.6 µm vs. WT-TGFβ3: 11.8 µm, V620I-BMP4: 12.5 µm, and T89I-BMP4: 11.3 µm; p < 0.0001; Figure 5A, B). This phenotype was not present in any of the groups from the V620I and T89I lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis and cell size measurements presented in Figure 5A-B.

claim: There was an increase in gene expression and protein production of hypertrophic cartilage markers COL10A1, ALPL, IHH, RUNX2 isoform 9 (RUNX2-9) in all three lines with BMP4 treatment; however, there was a stronger effect in WT.

claim: BMP4 treatment reduced MMP13 in the mutants but did not affect WT.

claim: The cluster 1 gene network is highly associated with ossification, biomineral tissue development, skeletal system development, tissue development, and osteoblast differentiation.

claim: ALPL, AMELX, FGFR3, IFITM5, IHH, PTH1R, and NOG were connected to at least 4 of the top 5 GO terms in the cluster 1 gene network.

claim: WT was highly associated with skeletal system development, ossification, endochondral ossification, and extracellular structure organization in GO term analysis of BMP4 up-regulated DEGs.

claim: V620I was associated with skeletal system development, ossification, endochondral ossification, and extracellular structure organization to a lesser degree than WT, while T89I showed little to no association.

claim: The TRPV4 mutations reduce BMP4-induced hypertrophy but to a greater extent with the T89I mutation.

claim: Day-28 chondrocytes exhibited differences in channel function and gene expression between the mutants and WT control.

claim: At the transcriptomic and proteomic levels, TRPV4 mutations inhibited chondrocyte hypertrophy, particularly with the T89I mutation, whereas V620I exhibited a milder phenotype.
source: At the transcriptomic and proteomic levels, TRPV4 mutations inhibited chondrocyte hypertrophy, particularly with the T89I mutation, whereas V620I exhibited a milder phenotype, consistent with the clinical presentation of these two conditions.

claim: Skeletal dysplasias may be, at least in part, resulting from improper chondrocyte hypertrophy downstream of altered TRPV4 function.
source: Our results suggest that skeletal dysplasias may be, at least in part, resulting from improper chondrocyte hypertrophy downstream of altered TRPV4 function.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: X. laevis oocytes injected with rat TRPV4 cRNA showed high basal currents in V620I.
source: Two other models that have studied the V620I and T89I mutations include X. laevis oocytes injected with rat TRPV4 cRNA (Loukin et al., 2011) or primary porcine chondrocytes transfected with human mutant TRPV4 (Leddy et al., 2014b). Both reports and our current study investigated the baseline currents of the mutant TRPV4 compared to WT. Here, we used patch clamping and observed high basal currents in V620I with a significant decrease when TRPV4 was inhibited. However, this characteristic was trending, but not significant, in T89I, despite both V620I and T89I being reported as gain-of-function mutations (Camacho et al., 2010; Rock et al., 2008). Both the X. laevis oocyte and porcine chondrocyte models confirmed high basal currents through V620I-TRPV4 (Leddy et al., 2014b; Loukin et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Primary porcine chondrocytes transfected with human mutant TRPV4 showed high basal currents in V620I.
source: Two other models that have studied the V620I and T89I mutations include X. laevis oocytes injected with rat TRPV4 cRNA (Loukin et al., 2011) or primary porcine chondrocytes transfected with human mutant TRPV4 (Leddy et al., 2014b). evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.
